factor_ratings.evidence: Leads engineering on the company's single embedded product line; impact contained to firmware and hardware bring-up team, not multiple functions or business-unit-level decisions.
Sets sprint priorities and reviews team output, but does not set overall technical strategy -- that is set jointly by the two co-founders. Direction is received from above on strategy.
Problems are scoped within the current product's firmware and integration issues; broader roadmap set elsewhere -- defined problem space, not open-ended or cross-domain.
Oversees firmware and hardware bring-up, adjacent disciplines, consistent with deep-in-one/credible-in-adjacent characterization; no evidence of company-wide sought-out authority.
Owns delivery of a single embedded product line's firmware/integration workstream across a development cycle -- subsystem-level ownership, not a platform or multi-generation roadmap.
Represents engineering in weekly leadership standups (peer/adjacent-function representation) but does not set or shape overall company technical strategy, which is reserved to co-founders.
8 direct reports, all individual contributors, matching the 4-10 IC-only range; no budget authority beyond headcount requisitions -- equipment and vendor spend approved by CFO.

decision.governing_rule: rule 6: title in the source document is evidence, not input -- level from described scope, never title
decision.alternative_reasoning: M4 was considered given the VP title and "leads all engineering," but span (8 ICs, no team leads), budget (none beyond requisitions), and autonomy (strategy set by co-founders, not this role) all fall below the M4 anchors (10-25 people, program budget ownership, function-wide program-setting). Scope of impact is not unambiguously at the higher level per rule 2, so the lower level (M3) governs.
decision.escalation_factor: span_and_budget vs. scope_of_impact -- if the company's small size means engineering leadership inherently carries more effective organizational weight than the raw headcount/budget numbers suggest, that could push toward M4
decision.reasoning: Despite the VP title, every scope factor points to M3: 8 direct reports all ICs (M3 span band), no budget authority beyond requisitions (explicitly M3 anchor language), problems scoped to a single product's firmware/integration issues (not strategic or open-ended), and technical strategy explicitly reserved to the co-founders rather than this role. Influence is limited to representing engineering in standups, not shaping business-unit or company strategy. Ownership is at the subsystem/single-product-line level (L4-equivalent under 5a), consistent with M3's L4 IC-equivalent mapping. All factors converge cleanly on M3 with no split requiring rule 2's lower-level tiebreak. Per section 6, source context (40-person growth-stage whole-company) sets a prior that titles at small companies map down 1-2 levels from nominal title level -- a "VP" mapping to M3 is consistent with that expected drift, so this result is consistent with (not contradicting) the prior, which raises confidence rather than lowering it.
